backlog.spec: Keep the RF, LightGBM and CatBoost members fitted once each as now, but make the variance-prone neural member stable by bagging it. Add to the ensemble an MLPClassifier (hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), early_stopping=True, max_iter=400) fitted three times with random_state = seed, seed+1, seed+2 on QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal')-scaled features; average the three MLP probability vectors into a single member score before rank-transforming. Then rank-average the four member scores (RF, LightGBM, CatBoost, bagged MLP) with equal weight. Everything else, including features, is unchanged.
backlog.title: Seed-bag only the unstable members

backlog.spec: The BBB dataset is class-imbalanced (roughly three quarters of molecules penetrate), and with scaffold-disjoint folds the minority class is what the ranking has to separate. Set balanced weighting in every member: RandomForestClassifier(class_weight='balanced_subsample'), LGBMClassifier(class_weight='balanced'), and CatBoostClassifier(auto_class_weights='Balanced'). Keep all features, all other hyperparameters and the rank-average aggregation exactly as they are, so the measurement isolates the effect of class weighting.
backlog.title: Balanced class weights across all ensemble members

backlog.spec: Change only the CatBoostClassifier settings inside fit_predict: depth=8, learning_rate=0.03, iterations=800, l2_leaf_reg=5, rsm=0.2, with the same thread_count and random_seed=seed. Keep the RF and LightGBM members and the rank average as they are. The aim is to test whether a deeper but more regularized booster helps.
backlog.title: Deeper, slower-learning CatBoost member

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment via rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser plus charge neutralization via rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, with a fallback to the original molecule on failure), and add two extra rank-averaged members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits (k=15) and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) on QuantileTransformer-scaled features. The experiment is one round of transductive self-training: fit the ensemble on the labelled training molecules, average the member probabilities (not ranks) on the test molecules, select test molecules whose averaged probability is above 0.9 or below 0.1, append them to the training set with hard labels 1 and 0 and a sample weight of 0.3 (training molecules get weight 1.0; pass sample_weight to every member that accepts it, and simply duplicate-free omit weighting for the kNN member), refit all members on the augmented set, and return the rank-average of the refitted members. Cap the number of pseudo-labels at 40 percent of the test set, keeping the most confident ones, and skip the second round entirely if fewer than 10 molecules pass the thresholds. Use the seed argument for all randomness and keep fit_predict's signature and the one-probability-per-test-molecule return contract.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training on the test molecules

backlog.spec: Change only the LGBMClassifier in fit_predict to extra_trees=True, min_child_samples=10, reg_lambda=1.0, with n_estimators=500 and learning_rate=0.05. Keep num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3, and n_jobs=8. The randomized split thresholds should act as extra regularization on the descriptor and fingerprint columns.
backlog.title: LightGBM with extra_trees and small min_child_samples

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment plus charge neutralization via rdMolStandardize, with a fallback), and add an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) member on QuantileTransformer-scaled features. The experiment is a stronger similarity-based member to replace a single-k Tanimoto kNN. Compute the full test-by-train Tanimoto similarity matrix on binary Morgan bits (radius 2, 2048 bits) with vectorized numpy, then form three scores per test molecule: the similarity-weighted label mean over the 5, 25 and 100 nearest training neighbours. Rank-transform each of the three and average them into one similarity score, and add that single score as a fourth rank-averaged member alongside the RF, LightGBM, CatBoost and the MLP. Also feed the maximum training similarity per test molecule nowhere else; do not use it as a feature. The rationale is that scaffold-split folds put test molecules at varying distances from the training set, so averaging over several neighbourhood radii is more robust than committing to one k. Keep the implementation to roughly twenty lines and seed everything from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Replace the single kNN with a multi-k similarity committee

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment plus charge neutralization via rdMolStandardize, with a fallback to the original molecule), and add two rank-averaged members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits (k=15) and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) on QuantileTransformer-scaled features. The experiment: wrap the whole five-member ensemble in a loop over three derived seeds (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000), rank-transform each member's test predictions within each repeat, and average all rank vectors across members and repeats. To stay inside the 10-minute budget, cut CatBoost to 300 iterations and LightGBM to 200 estimators and skip re-running the deterministic kNN member on repeats two and three. Seed bagging of the earlier three-member ensemble was flat, but the MLP is the highest-variance member in the new line-up, so the hypothesis is that averaging its seed noise is now worth the compute. Keep the code to a single outer loop and do not add any new feature blocks.
backlog.title: Multi-seed bagging of the adopted five-member ensemble

backlog.spec: Augment the training set with 2 extra copies of each training row. Add Gaussian noise with sd 0.05 times each descriptor column's training std to the descriptor columns only, and leave the Morgan counts unchanged. Labels stay the same. Fit all models on the augmented set. Use a seeded numpy Generator.
backlog.title: Descriptor noise augmentation

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment plus charge neutralization via rdMolStandardize, with a fallback), and add two rank-averaged members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True). The experiment gives the dense, distance-sensitive learners a feature view they can actually use: fit a TruncatedSVD with 128 components (seeded, fitted on the training fingerprint block only, then applied to the test block) to the 2048-column Morgan count matrix, and feed the MLP the concatenation of the QuantileTransformer-scaled RDKit descriptors and the 128 SVD components instead of the raw high-dimensional matrix. Leave the RF, LightGBM and CatBoost members on the original descriptor-plus-raw-count matrix, since trees handle sparse binary columns well, and leave the kNN member on binary Morgan bits. Keep the equal-weight rank-average blend. The hypothesis is that the MLP member is currently handicapped by 2048 sparse count columns and that a dense low-rank summary makes it a stronger, more decorrelated ensemble voice.
backlog.title: SVD-compressed fingerprint view for the dense learners

backlog.spec: Add one round of transductive self-training inside fit_predict. First fit the current three-member ensemble on the training data and produce rank-averaged scores for the test molecules as now. Then pick the confident test molecules: those whose averaged rank score is above 0.90 get pseudo-label 1 and those below 0.10 get pseudo-label 0 (cap the number taken at 30 percent of the test set, choosing the most extreme). Concatenate their feature rows and pseudo-labels to the training set with sample_weight 0.3 (training molecules weight 1.0), refit the same three members on the augmented set, and return the rank-average of the refitted members' test predictions. Use the seed for all model randomness and keep the total runtime under the 10-minute budget (roughly doubles the fit cost, which is acceptable).
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training on the test molecules

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment plus charge neutralization via rdMolStandardize, with a fallback), and add a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour member and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) member on QuantileTransformer-scaled features, both rank-averaged with the existing three. The experiment adds one genuinely different inductive bias as a further rank-averaged member: a KernelRidge (or RidgeClassifier equivalent on the kernel matrix) with kernel='precomputed' fitted on labels mapped to -1/+1, where the kernel is K = 0.5 * MinMax-Tanimoto(Morgan count vectors) + 0.5 * RBF(standardized descriptor columns, gamma = 1/n_descriptor_features), with alpha tuned over {0.1, 1.0} by a quick scaffold-grouped 3-fold inner split. With only about 1300 training molecules per fold the kernel matrices are small, so compute the MinMax Tanimoto with vectorized numpy minimum/maximum sums rather than loops. Rank-transform the kernel-ridge decision values before averaging. Note that precomputed-kernel SVCs on similar kernels were flat; the hypothesis here is that the smooth ridge fit, rather than the hinge loss, is what the ensemble is missing.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge on a combined Tanimoto plus descriptor-RBF kernel

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment plus charge neutralization via rdMolStandardize, with a fallback to the original molecule), and add two rank-averaged members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits (k=15) and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) on QuantileTransformer-scaled features. The experiment changes only the fingerprint block: replace the single radius-2 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprint with the concatenation of three count fingerprints at radius 1, 2 and 3, each hashed into 2048 bits (6144 fingerprint columns total, still appended after the RDKit descriptor block). Earlier single-scale swaps and a small-bit-space r1+r3 pair were flat, so the point here is that the extra multi-scale substructure channels need room not to collide. Keep colsample_bytree / rsm / max_features as fractions so each learner still sees a comparable absolute number of columns per split, and watch runtime: the job must finish 15 fits inside 10 minutes and 6 GB, so keep the fingerprint matrices float32 and reuse one generator per radius across all molecules.
backlog.title: Multi-scale Morgan counts in a larger bit space

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment plus charge neutralization via rdMolStandardize, with a fallback to the original molecule), and add two rank-averaged members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits (k=15) and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) on QuantileTransformer-scaled features. The experiment is input-noise regularization on the continuous part of the feature matrix. Build two extra noisy copies of the training set: for each copy, add Gaussian noise to the RDKit descriptor columns only (not the integer fingerprint counts) with per-column sd equal to 0.05 times that column's training standard deviation, leave the labels unchanged, and stack the three copies (original plus two noisy) into a 3x-sized training matrix. Fit the tree and boosting members and the MLP on the augmented matrix; leave the kNN member on the clean data. Test featurization is unchanged. Draw the noise from a numpy Generator seeded from the seed argument. Keep an eye on runtime, since tripling the rows roughly triples fit time: if needed drop CatBoost iterations to 300 so the 15 fits still finish inside 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Gaussian descriptor noise augmentation

backlog.spec: Replace the single radius-2 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprint with a multi-scale concatenation to give the trees both local and larger-environment features: radius 1 with 2048 count bits plus radius 3 with 2048 count bits, both appended after the RDKit descriptor block (so the feature vector becomes descriptors + 2048 + 2048). Keep the nan/inf cleanup and clipping, keep the three ensemble members and their hyperparameters, and keep the rank-average aggregation. If runtime becomes a concern, note that the RF max_features is a fraction so cost scales mildly with width.
backlog.title: Multi-scale Morgan counts in a larger bit space

backlog.spec: Rebuild train.py as the consolidated best-known configuration and run it to get a second measurement of it. In featurize, first standardize each molecule: parse the SMILES, keep only the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser or by splitting on '.' and taking the fragment with most heavy atoms), then neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger; if any step throws, fall back to the original parsed molecule. Keep the existing feature vector (all RDKit descList descriptors plus 2048-bit radius-2 Morgan counts, nan/inf cleaned and clipped). Keep the three existing members (RF, LightGBM, CatBoost) and add two more: (a) a Tanimoto kNN scorer on binary Morgan bits (radius 2, 2048 bits) that scores each test molecule as the mean label of its k=15 nearest training molecules weighted by Tanimoto similarity, and (b) an sklearn MLPClassifier (hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), early_stopping=True, max_iter=400, random_state=seed) on QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal')-scaled features. Rank-transform each member's test scores (rankdata/len) and take the plain mean of the five ranks.
backlog.title: Consolidated base: standardization + kNN + MLP (replicate)

backlog.spec: Regularize by augmenting the training set with jittered copies. After featurizing, split the feature matrix into the descriptor block (the leading len(Descriptors.descList) columns) and the fingerprint block. Compute per-column standard deviations of the descriptor block on the training rows. Then build two extra copies of the training set in which the descriptor columns get additive Gaussian noise of 0.05 times that per-column sd (fingerprint columns untouched, labels copied), using a numpy Generator seeded with the seed argument. Fit the existing RF, LightGBM and CatBoost members on the 3x-sized training matrix and keep the same rank-average of the three members for the untouched test matrix.
backlog.title: Gaussian noise augmentation of descriptor rows

backlog.spec: In featurize(), after the existing Morgan count fingerprint, append a 1024-bit Avalon count fingerprint computed with rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP(m, nBits=1024) converted to a numpy array with np.array(list(fp), dtype=np.float32). Keep the descriptors, Morgan counts, models, rank averaging and all hyperparameters unchanged. Only the feature matrix grows.
backlog.title: Append Avalon count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Set class_weight='balanced_subsample' in the RandomForest, is_unbalance=True (or class_weight='balanced') in LightGBM, and auto_class_weights='Balanced' in CatBoost. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Balanced class weights

backlog.spec: Build on the current train.py after adopting the two changes that already beat noise: standardize molecules inside featurize (largest fragment plus neutralization via rdMolStandardize, with a fallback), and add two extra members, a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour scorer on binary Morgan bits (k=15) and an MLPClassifier((256,64), early_stopping=True) on QuantileTransformer-scaled features, giving five members in total. The experiment replaces the equal-weight rank-average with learned non-negative weights. Inside fit_predict, compute Murcko scaffolds of the training molecules with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold, run a 5-fold GroupKFold over scaffold groups to get out-of-fold rank-transformed predictions for each member, then choose weights on the simplex that maximize out-of-fold AUROC by a coarse search: evaluate the 5 single-member corners, all equal-weight pairs and triples, and the uniform blend, and keep the best; shrink the winner halfway toward the uniform blend to guard against overfitting the inner split. Refit every member on the full training set and return the weighted rank-average on the test molecules. Keep the code compact (one helper for the member list, one for the weight search) and seed every member and the group split from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Blend weights tuned by scaffold-grouped inner CV

backlog.spec: Down-weight over-represented chemical series so the models do not overfit large scaffold families, which matters because every evaluation fold tests unseen Murcko scaffolds. In fit_predict, compute the Murcko scaffold SMILES of each training molecule with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles (empty string on failure), count how many training molecules share each scaffold, and set each molecule's weight to 1/sqrt(count), normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to all three members (RF, LightGBM, CatBoost) when fitting. Keep features, hyperparameters and the rank-average aggregation unchanged.
backlog.title: Inverse-scaffold-frequency sample weights

memo: Helped: only the slot 0 rank-average ensemble of RF, LightGBM and CatBoost on descriptors plus Morgan counts (0.1361 to 0.0942). Nothing else was accepted, yet several rejected ideas beat noise (sd about 0.0049): slot 15 kNN plus MLP (0.0868 and 0.0853 over 2 runs, -0.0081), slot 12 largest fragment plus neutralization (0.0899, -0.0043), slot 24 (0.0904), slot 26 weighted five-member blend (0.0901). Adopt these. Not helpful: fingerprint additions (atom-pair, path, MACCS, FCFP, EState), stacking, extra tree/SVC/HGB members, RF tweaks, monotone constraints, seed bagging (all within about ±0.002). Hurt: physchem-only (+0.0381), descriptors-only RF (+0.0152), single CatBoost (+0.0079), per-view RFs (+0.0032), dropping rare columns (+0.0029), logistic regression blend (+0.0137). Next: make slot 15 the base, add slot 12 standardization, then replicate. Then tune CatBoost/LightGBM depth and regularization. Avoid more stacking and fingerprint additions.
